answer.rationale: Write latency spike (5x target) in primary region started 90 minutes ago, coinciding with a release 2 hours ago. During active settlement peak with heavy writes, rollback is the fastest path to restore latency without risking write loss or requiring capacity decisions under high load. Memory b1 demonstrates rollback cleared a checkout error spike with no customer impact using the stable prior build. Memory b6 shows staged release gating catches regressions early—this suggests the release may contain the degradation. Current conditions (active writes, narrow intervention window, correlation with release timing) favor rollback over failover (which has latency recovery cost) or capacity add (slower and assumes capacity is the bottleneck, not the release). Circuit breaker and read routing do not address write path latency. Rollback preserves uncertainty about root cause while restoring service; we can investigate the release offline.
